detailed_rationale:
Akums Drugs & Pharmaceuticals is one of India's larger CDMO players (contract development and manufacturing across tablets, capsules, liquid orals, vials, ampoules, blow-fill-seal, topicals, eye drops, dry-powder injections and gummies). FY26 revenue grew modestly to Rs 4,359 Cr from Rs 4,118 Cr (+5.9%), but net profit fell to Rs 256 Cr from Rs 344 Cr (-25.6%) -- a genuine margin-compression story where the topline held up but profitability did not, which we flag as the key earnings-quality concern rather than a headline growth problem. Quarterly OPM has bounced between 9% and 13% over the last four quarters, without a clear recovering trend yet.

On the balance sheet, the picture is genuinely positive: borrowings have fallen sharply, from Rs 619 Cr (Mar 2023) to Rs 157 Cr (Mar 2026), making the company close to debt-free. Promoter holding is stable and high (75.26%). FII ownership has dropped sharply (7.34% to 1.91% since Sep 2024), a sentiment signal worth noting even though domestic institutions have picked up the slack (rising to 13.44%). A small bolt-on acquisition (Oriflame India's manufacturing operations, ~Rs 56 Cr, closing August 2026) is not large enough to move the thesis, and a previously-imposed penalty on a subsidiary was set aside on appeal -- a regulatory matter now resolved in the company's favour.

The core question for Akums is whether the FY26 margin compression is a temporary mix/pricing effect within CDMO contracts (where margins can be lumpy between segments and clients) or the start of a more structural pressure -- we did not find enough in the sources available to resolve that question either way, so our growth number reflects real caution on near-term earnings quality even as we credit the deleveraging and modest revenue growth.
recommendation_rationale: Hold, matching the quant score -- steady (if unspectacular) revenue growth and a much-improved balance sheet argue against a Sell, but a 25%+ profit decline despite revenue growth is a real margin-quality concern that keeps us from being more constructive than Hold.
summary: Akums Drugs & Pharmaceuticals, a large contract manufacturer for the pharma industry, grew revenue modestly in FY26 but saw profit fall by about a quarter as margins compressed, even as the company sharply reduced its debt. Foreign institutional ownership has declined notably over the past two years. We rate it a Hold: balance-sheet improvement is real, but the recent profit decline despite revenue growth needs to be watched closely.
positive_para: Debt has fallen dramatically (Rs 619 Cr to Rs 157 Cr over three years), promoter holding remains high and stable, and a previously-imposed regulatory penalty on a subsidiary was set aside on appeal. The CDMO/contract-manufacturing industry structurally benefits from pharma companies outsourcing production, giving the business a durable long-term demand base.
negative_para: FY26 net profit fell about 25.6% even as revenue grew nearly 6%, a clear margin-compression signal that has not yet shown a convincing recovery in the most recent quarters (OPM has ranged 9-13% without a clear upward trend). Foreign institutional holding has dropped sharply since late 2024 (7.34% to 1.91%), a sentiment signal that, while not conclusive on its own, is worth tracking alongside the margin question.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At roughly 42x earnings, the valuation is not cheap for a business whose profit just declined 25% on modest revenue growth; the multiple appears to assume the margin compression is temporary and will reverse. We do not have enough visibility from the sources available to confirm that reversal is already underway, so we would treat the current price as fully valued rather than a bargain until margins show a clearer recovery.
